correctness.rationale: For each bounded multiplier the increment-row test gives sup n|delta psi_n|<infinity. Every operator word in multipliers and parent composition has multiplier-times-shift normal form, and each commutator contributes a coefficient O(1/n). Products containing two commutators therefore have an O(1/n^2) coefficient and are compact by a tail-row bound O(1/n), proving the whole Calkin commutator ideal is square-zero after norm closure. The critical oscillatory family is verified via the exact finite-difference rows: B_m=(1-q^-1)^(m+1)U_qH modulo compacts. The Hardy operator has essential norm one by compact adjoint-row arguments. Abel cancellation gives HU_qH compact, yielding exact norm, nonzero square-zero witnesses and the sharp boundedness threshold. Finite checker results supplement, not replace, the proofs.

value.rationale: The commutator-generated ideal of the naturally generated operator algebra is nonzero yet has square zero in the Calkin quotient, which additionally becomes commutative after dividing by that ideal; this structural description is more informative than the norm of an individual operator. The sharp n^-1 multiplier threshold forces the explicit witnesses and gives a precise phase-dependent norm across all periodic and irrational unimodular modulations.
